name: Morgaine (Toreador Clan Leader of New Orleans)

system.concept: Ancient, possibly Druidic Toreador sculptor who leads through intimidation
system.title: Clan Leader (Toreador)
system.biography:
Background

Morgaine's true name and origin have long since faded even from her own memory; rumor holds she once studied with Wiccans or even ancient Druids, and her uncanny ability to terrify with a glance lends the stories credibility. The most visible @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} in New Orleans, she makes a point of personally meeting — and seducing — the most attractive newcomers to the city. A gifted musician and sculptor (some of her clay work hangs in museums under assumed names), she carries Play-Doh with her at all times, ostensibly for stress relief but really because idle hands invite the Beast. She owns the Lamp Light but keeps her true home in the Garden District, and leads New Orleans' @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} more through fear of her volatility than through any consensus of the clan, a fact that quietly rankles some of her clanmates. She is conspicuously absent from the Prince's Council, a standing detail that weakens that body's claim to speak for the city.

Roleplaying Hints

Outgoing and endlessly chatty about trivialities, but you turn abruptly serious — sparks practically flying from your eyes — the moment real business is at hand.

Disciplines (as printed, dot-rating, converted to owned Discipline Items on this Actor at Storyteller discretion): Auspex 4, Celerity 3, Dominate 4, Necromancy 1, Obfuscate 1, Presence 5, Protean 4, Thaumaturgy 2 (Lure of Flames 1, Movement of the Mind 1, Weather Control 1, Path of Conjuring 1, Path of Corruption 1).
system.notes: Sire: Jacques. Known rituals: Defense of the Sacred Haven, Wake with Morning's Freshness, Deflection of Wooden Doom, Rebirth of Mortal Vanity, Ward versus Ghouls. Haven: Garden District (owns the club the Lamp Light). Secrets rating: B.

system.description:
Named for the legendary (and supposedly fae) progenitor of the houses of Anjou and Lusignan, this power lets a Toreador sway others through song. If the Artisan can phrase her request in the form of a song, her words take on the weight of a nigh-irresistible command.

System: The player states the suggestion she wishes to weave into the song and describes the song's nature. Everyone within earshot must resist or unknowingly submit to the request. The effect lasts as long as the Toreador continues singing or until the target leaves her presence; commands requiring the victim to leave the singer's presence can be resisted once more after the enchanting voice fades. Listeners outside the Toreador's immediate presence may notice something odd about the performance, though it registers as little more than an exceptionally fine one; other Toreador within earshot are immediately entranced. As a side benefit, knowledge of this power makes the character a superlative singer even when the power itself is not invoked.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)
system.duration: As long as the Toreador continues singing, or until the target leaves her presence

items.name: Presence — 3 Advanced — Pulse of the City

system.description: Your emotional state is always passively mirrored by the population of an entire city-sized region, with visitors affected less strongly than residents and vampires affected one level more mildly than mortals. To deliberately project a chosen emotion, spend a Willpower Trait and win a Static Social Challenge (typically 10-15 Traits, Storyteller's call) to shift the city's mood for one minute, extendable by spending additional Social Traits before the challenge. Two Methuselahs with this power contesting the same city test the Social Challenge directly against one another, with the longer-established Methuselah (six months or more) gaining five bonus Traits. Usable even while in torpor.
system.bloodCost: One Willpower Trait (plus Social Traits to extend duration)
system.duration: One minute per activation, longer with extra Social Traits spent

system.description:
A diplomat's most difficult task is understanding what people need to hear to make them agreeable to a suggestion. With this power, a Toreador learns what a target wants to hear. It does not reveal the target's full views, but it grants invaluable insight that can be put to use in negotiation, avoiding treachery, or worse — enemies may be allied, marriages arranged, and wars started with proper application of this knack.

System: The character concentrates on her subject and, on success, knows what to say to elicit a particular response. If she is attempting to advance an idea the target believes fundamentally wrong (convincing a pacifist monk to propose war, or a happy person to consider suicide), the target may resist. The effect lasts for the remainder of the conversation.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

system.description: By winning a Mental Challenge while holding your victim's gaze, you can erase, alter, or implant up to fifteen minutes of memory per challenge, or question the subject to recall details they otherwise might not share.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Over several consecutive nights of unrestricted access and repeated Mental Challenges, you can break down a victim's will entirely, turning them into a virtually mindless thrall who obeys you without need for further tests.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.

By this gift, a Toreador may penetrate the "soul" of an inanimate artwork she examines, interpreting the piece, gleaning the artist's state of mind, the relationship between artist and work, and the stages of the creative process, revealed as a series of progressively paler images looking back into the work's history. Some Toreador use this to critique or authenticate a piece; others monitor their proteges' work for unspoken rebellion or sadness, or seek the "real" story behind a letter proposing an alliance. The power does not function on "living" art still in the act of performance — a play, a song, or a story being told — since such work depends on the performer's ongoing intent rather than a fixed, finished creation.

System: The character examines the work and the number of successes determines how much she perceives: a single success yields only general feelings with no historical context; two successes offer a vague sense of the work's history; three successes reveal specific details and a fuzzy timeline; four successes grant a definite sense of the artist's emotional state and a reasonable timeline; five successes let the Toreador see the work in stages, feeling what the artist felt at every step of its creation. The difficulty rises for pieces with multiple artists or a long creation span; examining something as vast as a cathedral or castle risks leaving the Toreador a gibbering wreck from informational overload.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

items.name: Protean — 2 Intermediate — Shape of the Beast

system.description: By spending one to three Blood Traits over one to three turns, you transform into an animal form such as a wolf or bat, gaining its natural advantages and the use of most of your other Disciplines, until the next dawn or until you change back.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines
system.duration: Until next dawn or you choose to revert

system.description: By spending a Blood Trait and a full turn, you sink into raw soil, becoming undetectable and immune to daylight while you sleep undisturbed, rising again at will or if the soil is disturbed.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

vtmlarp.source: New Orleans by Night, Chapter Four: Characters
